title: /edit cannot open a prompt that was typed before it
body:
`/edit` (d2094e5) opens the prompt in `$VISUAL`, then `$EDITOR`, then `vi`, with coax suspended. Because a command must start the prompt, typing `/edit` replaces whatever was there. So the editor opens on the text typed after the command name, as in `/edit some draft`, or empty for a bare `/edit`. There is no way to edit a long prompt already typed, which is the main reason to reach for an editor.

## Options

- A key that opens the whole current prompt in the editor, as Ctrl+g does in some shells and agents. Lean: this one. It needs a key, and keys are versioned, so it moves the minor version. Jack dislikes key actions, so it is his call.
- `/edit` keeps the prompt as it was before the user started typing the command. coax remembers the text when the prompt changes from not starting with `/` to starting with it, and offers that text to the editor. That uses no key, but the behaviour is invisible.
- Leave `/edit` as it is.
